_doc: Codex Rites page, Age Wardens. Same shape as ritual_hints.json; text equals the in-game clue.

hints.text: The first hearth was ringed with flint. Sixteen chips, laid at the foot of the stone.
The walking dead guard the old fire-ring. Let six fall in sight of the altar.
Trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: the gate the Fair Folk keep; then kin of the tree that holds up the world.
The stone will answer only in the breath between night and the first light. Use the altar then.
Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 30 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.
The green metal came before the bright one. Sixteen ingots, warm from the pot.
Bone-archers keep the ore roads. Ten must be unstrung.
Trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: the gate the Fair Folk keep; then the pale one that wears the first white.
The stone will answer only as the sun drowns and the first stars wake. Use the altar then.
Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 40 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.
The altar eats before it fights. Set one feast upon the stone, a dish worth a guest-gift.
Two soft metals made one hard. Eight bronze bars upon the stone.
The weavers of the dark hollows resent the smiths. Twelve of them fewer.
Trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: red berries set against the witch; then the gate the Fair Folk keep; then red berries set against the witch.
The stone will answer only when no shadow falls beside the stone. Use the altar then.
Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 45 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.
The altar eats before it fights. Set one feast upon the stone, a dish worth a guest-gift.
The grey metal rings truer than the bronze. Twenty-four ingots, cold and plain.
The brewers who sold the smiths their ruin. Five must answer.
Trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: kin of the tree that holds up the world; then the pale one that wears the first white; then the weeper by the water.
The stone will answer only when the moon stands highest over the stone. Use the altar then.
Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 60 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.
The altar eats before it fights. Set one feast upon the stone, a dish worth a guest-gift.
Iron taught to bend and not break. Eight steel bars for the warden's gate.
The hissing ones undo what smiths make. Fifteen must be put out.

Trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: the nut of the one who knows; then the weeper by the water; then kin of the tree that holds up the world; then the gate the Fair Folk keep.
The stone will answer only in the breath between night and the first light. Use the altar then.
It will not wake for one hand. 2 must stand at the altar together, or the stone will take a token for every spirit that stands in for a friend.
Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 75 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.
The altar eats before it fights. Set one feast upon the stone, a dish worth a guest-gift.
The late age runs on red dust and wire. Eight blocks, packed and dull.
Tall walkers step between the wires. Eight must lose their footing.

Trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: the winter king, green when all is grey; then red berries set against the witch; then the one that bleeds when it is cut; then the door-wood, the strong one.
The stone will answer only when no shadow falls beside the stone. Use the altar then.
It will not wake for one hand. 2 must stand at the altar together, or the stone will take a token for every spirit that stands in for a friend.
Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 90 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.
The altar eats before it fights. Set one feast upon the stone, a dish worth a guest-gift.
The last Age answers in echoes. Six shards, still ringing.
Sleepless watchers circle the end of days. Twelve must fall.

Trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: the weeper by the water; then the nut of the one who knows; then kin of the tree that holds up the world; then the nut of the one who knows; then the gate the Fair Folk keep.
The stone will answer only when the moon stands highest over the stone. Use the altar then.
It will not wake for one hand. 3 must stand at the altar together, or the stone will take a token for every spirit that stands in for a friend.
